documents.title: Leadership Brief
documents.summary: Guidance for church leadership on decision-making, scale, and stewardship for stage productions.
documents.content:
“Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.” — Proverbs 15:22

Leadership Brief: Guiding Stage Ministry Decisions

Purpose

To help pastors and ministry leaders make informed, prayerful decisions about pageant scope, volunteer load, and creative direction.

Decision Priorities

  1. Mission Alignment - Every performance must reinforce the church's vision and theology.
  2. Stewardship - Consider budget, facility use, and volunteer capacity before committing to scope or schedule.
  3. Safety & Sustainability - Favor smaller, consistent excellence over large, exhausting undertakings.
  4. Accessibility - Aim for clarity of message; avoid complexity that distracts from the Gospel.

Leadership Checklist

  • [ ] Script/theme approved by pastoral team
  • [ ] Budget & resources confirmed
  • [ ] Volunteer coordinator assigned
  • [ ] Safety plan reviewed
  • [ ] Post-event evaluation scheduled

documents.title: Theology Of Art
documents.summary: Biblical foundation for creativity and the arts in worship.
documents.content:
Creativity is not decoration — it is declaration.

Theology of Art and Creativity

God as Creator

Art exists because God is creative. From Genesis 1 onward, creation reveals design, order, and beauty that reflect His nature.

Creativity as Worship

When we paint, act, sing, or build sets, we echo the Creator. Our goal is not self-expression but God-expression — revealing His truth through beauty.

Biblical References

  • Exodus 31:1-5 - Bezalel filled with the Spirit to craft the tabernacle.
  • Psalm 33:3 - “Sing to Him a new song.”
  • Colossians 3:23 - “Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord.”

Application

Every creative act in ministry should:

  1. Glorify God
  2. Edify the Church
  3. Invite others into worship

documents.title: Vision
documents.summary: Purpose and vision behind church stage productions.
documents.content:
“Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.” — Colossians 3:23

Vision and Purpose

Every performance we create is a ministry — a visible act of worship that communicates God's story. Our goal is not entertainment but revelation: that through story, song, and movement, audiences encounter truth, grace, and hope.

Why We Perform

  • To glorify God with the gifts He has entrusted to us.
  • To teach biblical truth through creative expression.
  • To unify diverse volunteers under one mission: sharing the Gospel.
  • To serve our congregation and community with excellence and humility.
